ABOUT.LABEL: About/>
ABOUT.L2: Rendering engineer with electrical-engineering roots and a product-first mindset.
ABOUT.ROLE: I work on real-time rendering, procedural terrain pipelines and the tooling around them.
ABOUT.H1_L1: Moved from freelance video to frontend; combine creative work and engineering to deliver dependable results.
ABOUT.H1_L2: Grew and led an Arma 3 community of 150+; built attendance and ranking systems and coordinated events.
ABOUT.H1_L3: Reworked Arma mod loading—reduced total mod load by ~70% and improved client/server load times and runtime performance.
ABOUT.H2_L1: Build large-scale procedural terrain pipelines from OpenStreetMap data and optimize workflows for very large environments.
ABOUT.H2_L2: Built and run armasrbija.rs—combining backend, frontend, and deployment for community and game services.
ABOUT.H2_L3: Open to roles and contracts with clear ownership, pipeline optimization, and measurable impact.
ABOUT.LANGS_INLINE: Languages: C, C++, Python, Java, C#, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, SQL
ABOUT.TOOLS_INLINE: Tools: Angular, Svelte, Node.js, Tailwind, Git, Docker, SQLite, Cloudflare, Linux
ABOUT.TITLE: Electrical-engineering roots, product-first habits.
ABOUT.P1: I came to rendering through games and community infrastructure rather than a graphics course. Running a 150-person Arma 3 unit taught me that a frame that hitches on someone else’s machine is a bug, not an opinion, and most of what I build since is in service of that.
ABOUT.P2: Novi Sad, Serbia. Remote or hybrid, CET. Open to roles and contracts with clear ownership and a number I can move.

HOME.TITLE: The frame budget is the spec.
HOME.SUBTITLE: Everything below runs inside a fixed time slice, on hardware I do not get to choose. That constraint is the interesting part — it turns rendering, terrain generation and tooling into the same problem wearing three different hats.

STACK.TITLE: $stack

RENDER.TITLE: Real-time rendering
RENDER.BODY: Shader authoring, lighting and the profiling loop around them. The hero above is the working example: raymarched, dynamically scaled, and instrumented with the same timer that decides its resolution.

TERRAIN.TITLE: Procedural terrain
TERRAIN.BODY: Large-scale terrain built from OpenStreetMap data — heightfield generation, LOD, and the import pipeline that has to survive environments far bigger than memory.

SYSTEMS.TITLE: Systems & tooling
SYSTEMS.BODY: The unglamorous half. Reworking Arma 3 mod loading cut total load by roughly 70%, which came from measurement and a build step, not from a clever renderer.
